:::{.proof}
Let $x \in A$.
By @def-argmax, $x \in \argmax_{x \in A} c\,g(x)$
[if and only if](proof-writing.qmd#def-iff)
$c\,g(a) \le c\,g(x)$ for every $a \in A$.

Suppose $g(a) \le g(x)$.
If $g(a) = g(x)$, then $c\,g(a) = c\,g(x)$.
If $g(a) < g(x)$, then $c\,g(a) < c\,g(x)$ by @thm-mult-ineq.
Either way, $c\,g(a) \le c\,g(x)$.

Conversely, suppose $c\,g(a) \le c\,g(x)$.
Apply the same reasoning with $1/c > 0$ in place of $c$:
this gives $g(a) \le g(x)$.

So $c\,g(a) \le c\,g(x)$ for every $a \in A$ if and only if $g(a) \le g(x)$ for every $a \in A$.
Hence $x$ is in the [argmax](#def-argmax) of $c\,g$ exactly when it is in the argmax of $g$.
:::
